title: Planned vs predicted date chart per goal and milestone
subtitle: Mock-ups for issue #1801: how far a goal or milestone drifts and which feature drives it. Invented data. Switches: ?pc1=a|b|c, ?pc2=a|b|c, ?pc3=a|b|c, &mkdata=big, &open=1.

decisions.name: Chart form and place
decisions.question: Which chart shows planned against predicted dates, and where does it live?
decisions.common: Every proposal reads the same dates: the due date as an open diamond, the predicted date as a filled dot, and the words late, on time or early beside them (a shape and a word, never colour alone). Each names the feature that sets the predicted date with its code, and that name opens the one feature panel. It only reads: owners, approvers, commenters and viewers all see the same. Today nothing shows how far a goal drifts.

proposals.name: Dates on goal cards
proposals.what: On the Goal map, each goal card gets one thin line under its progress bar: the due date, the predicted date, the gap between them and a late or early word. A click opens a small panel with the same line for the goal and for each of its milestones, each naming the feature that sets its date.
proposals.why: The Goal map already shows goals over their milestones, so the dates sit where people read goals; one line per item reads at a glance, and the panel covers the milestones too.
proposals.plus: No new page or tab; the milestone lines answer 'in the milestone panel' in the same place.
proposals.cost: 0 clicks to see late or early on every goal; 1 click for the milestones; 2 clicks to reach the feature. Today: not possible.

frames.caption: At rest: each goal card shows its due date, its predicted date and 4 days early, 12 days late, or No date yet.
One click on the Paid conversions line opens its dates: the goal and its three milestones, each with the feature that sets the date.
The pointer is on F-107 Partner referral channel, the feature that sets the goal's date.
That click opens F-107's own feature panel, its dates Dec 16 to Jan 12; the corner shows the cost.
The hard case at 1512: twenty features and four milestones; the card still shows one line, the panel four.
On a phone the dates open as a sheet above the tab bar.

proposals.name: Weekly drift on Roadmap
proposals.what: On the Roadmap's goal cards, a small line of the predicted date week by week against the flat due date, so you see when it started to slip. A click opens a larger chart with the weeks named and the feature that sets the date.
proposals.plus: Shows when the slip began, not only how big it is.
proposals.cost: 0 clicks for the trend on each card; 1 click for the weeks; 2 to reach the feature. Milestones are not shown.

frames.caption: At rest: each Roadmap goal card has a small weekly line with 4 days early or 12 days late.
One click on Paid conversions opens its predicted date by week against the Dec 31 due date.
The pointer is on F-107 Partner referral channel.
That click opens F-107 on the Roadmap, its bar now Dec 16 to Jan 12.
The hard case at 1512: twenty features move the date from Feb 26 to Mar 9 over eight weeks.
On a phone the weekly chart opens as a sheet.

proposals.name: Slip bars on milestones
proposals.what: On the Goal map's milestone strip, each milestone gets a short bar as long as its slip, with +9 days, On time or No date. A click opens that milestone's dates and the feature that sets them. The goal itself has no line.
proposals.plus: Points straight at the milestone that slips.
proposals.cost: 0 clicks to see each milestone's slip; 1 click per milestone; 2 to reach the feature. No one line for the goal.

frames.caption: At rest: each milestone chip ends with its slip: 2 days early, +9 days, +12 days, No date.
One click on M4's +9 days opens its due and predicted dates.
The pointer is on F-108 Pricing page test, which sets M4's date.
That click opens F-108's panel, its dates Nov 12 to Dec 9.
The hard case at 1512: the strip's chips wrap in narrow goal columns.
On a phone the slip words wrap and the dates open as a sheet.

decisions.name: What predicted says
decisions.question: What is the predicted date read from, and how are its confidence and reason shown?
decisions.common: Every proposal shows late, on time, early, or No date yet when no feature has an end date, with a word and a shape. The reason and confidence sit behind an (i) or a tooltip, never a paragraph. All are drawn on the Goal map's goal cards.

proposals.name: Latest end, (i) why
proposals.what: The predicted date is the latest end date among the goal's features. The card shows the date and late or early; the (i) in its panel says what it is read from, which feature ends last, and how many features have an end date.
proposals.why: It is the rule a person can check by hand from the feature panels, and the count of undated features says how far to trust it.
proposals.plus: Uses only the end dates the Roadmap already has.
proposals.cost: 1 click for the dates, 1 more on the (i) for why: 2 clicks.

frames.caption: At rest: one goal early, one late, one with No date yet.
The Paid conversions dates with the (i) open: read from the latest feature end date, F-107 ends Jan 12, 4 of 5 features have an end date.
The pointer is on F-107, the feature that ends last.
F-107's panel opens with its end date Jan 12, the same date as the prediction.
The hard case at 1512: 18 of 20 features have an end date.
On a phone the same reason sits behind the (i) in the sheet.

proposals.name: Range from past slips
proposals.what: The predicted date is shown as a range, not a day: the latest end date widened by how far the team's past features ended past their plan (the stored predicted-against-actual records) and by how many features have no end date. A wide band means less sure.
proposals.plus: Confidence is drawn, not just said.
proposals.cost: 0 clicks to read the range; 2 clicks for why. The range is harder to quote than one date.

frames.caption: At rest: each card shows a hatched band, e.g. Due Dec 31 · Jan 5 – Jan 19.
The dates opened with the (i) showing what the range is read from.
The pointer is on F-107, the feature that ends last.
F-107's panel opens.
The hard case at 1512: two undated features widen the band.
On a phone the band and its dates wrap under the card.

proposals.name: Status tick only
proposals.what: No chart on the card: a single tick (a check for on time or early, a warning for late, a dash for no date) beside the due date; its tooltip and a click give the predicted date and the feature that sets it.
proposals.plus: The quietest card; nothing new to learn.
proposals.cost: 1 click on the tick to read any date at all; 2 to reach the feature.

frames.caption: At rest: a check, a warning or a dash beside each goal's due date.
One click on the warning: 12 days late, due Dec 31, predicted Jan 12.
The pointer is on F-107 Partner referral channel.
F-107's panel opens.
The hard case at 1512 looks the same as the easy one: the tick hides how many milestones slip.
On a phone the tick opens a short sheet.

decisions.name: Twenty features, four milestones
decisions.question: How does a goal with twenty features and four milestones stay readable at 1512 and on a phone?
decisions.common: Every proposal opens from the goal card's one line, uses the app's pass, warn and crit colours with a shape and a word for each (readable without colour), works in light and dark, and keeps the panel inside the window with its own scroll.

proposals.name: One line per milestone
proposals.what: The panel shows the goal's line, then one line per milestone, each naming only the one feature that sets its date; the count of undated features closes it.
proposals.why: Four milestones fit without scrolling at 1512; the reader sees which milestone slips and which feature to open, and twenty features never crowd the view.
proposals.plus: Same look as the small case, so nothing new to learn.
proposals.cost: 1 click for all four milestones; 1 more for the feature. Other features are one more click away, in their milestone.

frames.caption: At rest: twenty features, the goal 11 days late.
One click: the goal and M2, M4, M7, M9 each on one line with the feature that sets it.
The pointer is on F-108 Pricing page test, which sets M4.
F-108's panel opens, its dates Nov 12 to Dec 9.
At 1512 the whole panel fits; the frame's dark copy is beside it (?theme=dark).
On a phone the four lines scroll inside the sheet.

proposals.name: Every feature a tick
proposals.what: Each milestone line also carries a small tick for every feature's end date; the feature that sets the date is a thick tick and is named.
proposals.plus: Shows the spread: one late outlier or many late features.
proposals.cost: 1 click; reading twenty ticks takes longer, and close ticks merge on a phone.

frames.caption: At rest: the goal card's line carries twenty thin ticks.
One click: each milestone line with its features' ticks, the one that sets its date thick.
The pointer is on F-108 Pricing page test.
F-108's panel opens.
At 1512 in dark: ticks stay apart; colour is backed by thickness.
On a phone the ticks crowd together.

proposals.name: Ranked by days late
proposals.what: Under the goal's line, the features are listed by how many days they push past their milestone's date, with a bar for each; six show, Show all 20 lists the rest.
proposals.plus: Answers 'what do we fix first' directly.
proposals.cost: 1 click for the top six, 1 for all 20, 1 to open a feature: 3 clicks. Milestones are not drawn.

frames.caption: At rest: the goal card shows 11 days late.
One click: the six features that push the date most, +20 days at the top.
Show all 20 lists every feature; the pointer is on F-107 Partner referral channel.
F-107's panel opens.
At 1512 the ranked list fits beside the goal line.
On a phone in dark: names shorten, the days stay readable.
